items.title: Luther's Bible and standard German
items.claim: Martin Luther's complete German Bible was published in which year, and which dialect did it draw on as a base?

options.text: 1534, drawing on the East Central German of the Saxon chancellery

items.reveal_title: 1534, based on chancellery East Central German
items.reveal:
Luther's New Testament appeared in 1522; the complete Bible in 1534. The work spread widely with printing and influenced the form of Standard German over the following centuries.

Mid-19th-century unification of orthography accelerated the standard's reach.
items.why: A widely read religious translation can shape a literary language for centuries.

items.title: When the Grimms began publishing
items.claim: The first edition of the Brothers Grimm's Kinder- und Hausmarchen appeared in which year?
items.reveal:
Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected tales partly from middle-class informants of Huguenot background, including Dorothea Viehmann.

Later editions softened violence in some tales. Their later Deutsches Worterbuch project was completed only in 1961.
items.why: The 'folk' in folklore is often more bourgeois and literate than the framing implies.

items.title: Kant's three critiques
items.claim: Immanuel Kant published three critiques. Which is correct?

options.text: Of Pure Reason (1781), of Practical Reason (1788), of the Power of Judgement (1790)
Of Logic (1700), of Politics (1750), of Religion (1800)
Of Knowledge (1850), of Art (1900), of Science (1950)

items.reveal:
Kant rarely left Konigsberg, but his work reshaped European philosophy. His 1784 essay 'Was ist Aufklarung?' coined a defining slogan: 'Sapere aude'.

The second edition of the first critique (1787) is the version standardly cited.
items.why: Philosophical revolutions can be carried out at a desk in a provincial city.

items.title: 1996 spelling reform
items.claim: A German spelling reform was agreed in 1996 and implemented in stages. Which change is genuinely part of it?

options.text: Abolition of capital letters on nouns
Replacing ß with ss after short vowels in many words (e.g. dass instead of daß)

items.reveal:
The reform rationalised ss usage according to vowel length, modified some compound spellings and changed comma rules.

Major newspapers reversed and re-adopted parts of the reform in the early 2000s, settling on a revised version by 2006.
items.why: Orthographic reforms often face strong public reaction and partial reversal.

items.title: Yiddish speaker numbers
items.claim: Yiddish is a West Germanic language historically spoken by Ashkenazi Jews. About how many speakers worldwide today?
items.reveal_title: Around three quarters of a million today
items.reveal:
Ethnologue and YIVO estimates suggest between roughly 600,000 and 1 million speakers, concentrated in Hasidic communities in the US, Israel, the UK and elsewhere.

Before 1939, estimates suggested over 11 million speakers.
items.why: Catastrophic 20th-century events shaped which Germanic languages survived in numbers.

items.title: The longest German word in use
items.claim: German allows long noun compounds. A famous legal-administrative example abolished in 2013 was:
items.reveal:
The cattle-marking-and-beef-labelling-supervision-duties-delegation-law was repealed in 2013, partially because EU rules changed.

The Duden does not generally treat such legal compounds as 'words' for dictionary purposes.
items.why: Morphological possibility is not the same as everyday usage.

items.title: Klemperer's LTI
items.claim: Victor Klemperer's LTI: Notizbuch eines Philologen (1947) studied which subject?

options.text: The language of the Third Reich, observed during the war by a Romance philologist who survived persecution

items.reveal_title: A close linguistic analysis of Nazi-era German
items.reveal:
Klemperer (Romanist at Dresden, dismissed in 1935) compiled a study of Nazi-period vocabulary, rhetoric and propaganda forms.

The book has remained continuously in print as a model of linguistic study under dictatorship.
items.why: Documentary records of how a regime uses language can outlast the regime itself.

items.title: Where German is spoken
items.claim: German is an official or co-official language of how many European countries?

options.text: Six (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Belgium)

items.reveal_title: Six European states give German official status
items.reveal:
It is the sole official language in Liechtenstein and one of multiple in Belgium (East Cantons), Luxembourg, Switzerland and Italy's South Tyrol.

German is the most widely spoken native language in the EU (around 95 million).
items.why: Language geography rarely matches state borders neatly.

items.title: When the Duden first appeared
items.claim: Konrad Duden's first orthographic dictionary was published in which year?
items.reveal:
Duden's Vollstandiges Orthographisches Worterbuch der deutschen Sprache appeared in Leipzig in 1880.

A standard Orthographische Konferenz in 1901 made it the de facto national reference, a role it has held since.
items.why: Standardisation of writing systems was a late 19th-century project across Europe.

items.title: Swiss German diglossia
items.claim: German-speaking Switzerland uses Swiss German dialects for everyday speech and Standard German for which contexts?

options.text: Most writing, school instruction and formal broadcasting; daily speech remains dialect

items.reveal:
Linguists describe Swiss German as a textbook case of diglossia. Standard German is used for most written and formal contexts; dialect dominates speech, including on regional television.

Swiss German varieties differ substantially from one canton to another.
items.why: A community can run two registers of a language indefinitely in parallel.

items.title: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt
items.claim: Bertolt Brecht's theatre theory is widely translated as 'alienation effect'. What does Verfremdungseffekt specifically aim to do?

options.text: Make audiences identify completely with characters
Disrupt emotional immersion so the audience thinks critically about the social conditions depicted
Make plays as short as possible

items.reveal:
Brecht developed the concept from the late 1920s. Verfremdung is closer to 'making strange' than to ordinary alienation.

The Berliner Ensemble, founded with Helene Weigel in 1949, became its main institutional home.
items.why: Translation choices can shift the apparent meaning of a theoretical term.

items.title: East German vocabulary after 1990
items.claim: After German reunification (1990), East German specific vocabulary largely faded. One word that survived in widespread use is:
items.reveal_title: The Ampelmannchen survived as a cultural icon
items.reveal:
Created in 1961 by Karl Peglau, the East Berlin pedestrian-light figure was retained after unification following public campaigns.

Most specifically DDR-era political vocabulary disappeared from active use within a decade.
items.why: Symbols can outlive the political contexts that created them.
